Centre for Trade Excellence Participates in ASEAN Summit Milestone on Strategic Trade Management
Manila, Philippines | 15 November 2026

The Centre for Trade Excellence was honoured to participate as a collaborating institution in a side event held in conjunction with the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, marking the adoption of the ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Strategic Trade Management for Secure Regional Trade.

The Declaration represents an important development in ASEAN's approach to economic security. It reflects a growing recognition that safeguarding international trade and maintaining open, competitive markets are not competing objectives. Rather, both are essential to the region's continued prosperity, technological advancement and integration into global supply chains.
‍
For ASEAN, whose economic strength rests substantially on its connectivity with global markets, the responsible management of strategic and dual-use items is increasingly important. Effective strategic trade management can strengthen confidence among trading partners, protect legitimate commerce and reinforce the region's standing as a trusted manufacturing and investment destination.
‍
From Regional Commitment to Institutional Cooperation
‍
The significance of the Declaration lies not only in the principles it affirms, but also in the institutional arrangements it establishes to support their implementation.
‍
Notably, ASEAN Leaders agreed to establish an ASEAN Expert Group on Strategic Trade Management (AEGSTM) under the ASEAN Economic Community framework.
‍
The Expert Group will provide a voluntary regional platform for technical dialogue, information-sharing, the exchange of good practices and capacity-building. It will also support the development of a roadmap for strengthening strategic trade management and regional cooperation, while recognising differences in national circumstances, institutional capacities and levels of readiness.
‍
This approach reflects an important feature of ASEAN cooperation: the ability to pursue common objectives while respecting national sovereignty and accommodating different stages of institutional development.
‍
The Declaration also recognises the role of industry and the private sector in promoting compliance and maintaining secure, trusted supply chains. Their engagement will be essential in translating policy commitments into practices that are both effective and commercially workable.
‍
Bridging Policy Leadership and Practical Implementation
‍
Against this backdrop, our President delivered a presentation entitled Strengthening Economic Security: Bridging Policy Leadership and STM Practice.
‍
The presentation examined the relationship between regional economic security priorities and the practical requirements of effective strategic trade management.
‍
While political commitments provide direction, their implementation depends on national legal and regulatory frameworks, capable institutions, effective interagency coordination and meaningful engagement with industry.
‍
These considerations are particularly relevant in Southeast Asia, where national strategic trade management systems differ in their development, institutional arrangements and operational capabilities.
‍
The challenge ahead is therefore not simply to encourage greater regulatory alignment, but to develop practical avenues for cooperation that strengthen national capabilities while supporting ASEAN's broader economic integration.
‍
Supporting ASEAN's Evolving Economic Security Architecture
‍
The Centre welcomes the leadership demonstrated by the Philippines in advancing this important regional initiative and acknowledges the constructive engagement of international partners in supporting ASEAN's capacity-building and cooperation efforts.
‍
The Declaration provides an opportunity to deepen technical exchanges, strengthen institutional relationships and develop practical responses to emerging trade security risks.
‍
It also reinforces the importance of sustained dialogue among policymakers, regulatory authorities, industry and other stakeholders. Effective strategic trade management requires more than sound legislation. It depends on the ability of institutions and businesses to understand their responsibilities, identify risks and respond appropriately within an increasingly complex trading environment.
‍
As ASEAN moves from commitment to implementation, the Centre looks forward to contributing its expertise and supporting practical cooperation towards a more secure, resilient and prosperous region.
‍
